exposure: Early breastfeeding behaviors (initiation, frequency, duration, formula supplement, infant sucking performance)
cohort: A total of 648 healthy breastfeeding primiparas (333 delivered by CS, and 315 by vaginal birth) recruited from three teaching hospitals.
finding: Cesarean section had an unadjusted detrimental effect on early breastfeeding behaviors and long-term breastfeeding outcomes, but this negative effect on long-term breastfeeding was attenuated and no longer significant after adjusting for early breastfeeding behaviors.
mod_finding: Cesarean section itself was not found to be a negative factor for long-term breastfeeding outcomes when early breastfeeding behaviors were accounted for, suggesting that early feeding difficulties rather than the mode of birth per se lead to long-term problems.
